source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"A full, months-long orientation matching what a brand-new permanent hire would typically receive over their first several weeks","B":"Facility-specific orientation covering essential policies, procedures, and unit-specific information, even if abbreviated","C":"Orientation provided mainly if the agency nurse happens to ask for it upon arrival to the unit","D":"Very little orientation, on the assumption that agency staff already know most of what they need going in"}}
source_row.rationale: Facilities should ensure agency nurses receive facility-specific orientation covering essential policies, procedures, and unit-specific information, even if abbreviated compared to a new permanent hire.
source_row.source_name: The Joint Commission — Contract/Agency Staff Orientation Standards

source_row.stem: A hospital's onboarding process for a new travel nurse should include verification of:
source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Mainly a check of the nurse's travel arrangements and lodging rather than their professional qualifications","B":"Fairly minimal credentialing verification, on the assumption that the staffing agency handles most of that step","C":"Little more than a short introduction to the physical layout of the unit itself","D":"Licensure, certifications, and competency, along with facility-specific orientation"}}
source_row.rationale: Travel nurse onboarding should include verification of licensure, relevant certifications, and competency, along with facility-specific orientation, ensuring the same safety standards apply as for other staff.
source_row.source_name: The Joint Commission — Temporary Staff Credentialing Standards

source_row.stem: A hospital's nurse residency program seeks accreditation to demonstrate quality and adherence to established standards. This accreditation may be sought through organizations such as:
source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"A body unrelated to nursing education","B":"The American Nurses Credentialing Center (ANCC) Practice Transition Accreditation Program","C":"No accreditation bodies exist for nurse residency programs","D":"Only state licensing boards, with no national accreditation available"}}
source_row.rationale: Nurse residency programs may seek accreditation through organizations such as the ANCC Practice Transition Accreditation Program, demonstrating adherence to established quality standards.

source_row.stem: A nurse explains the general difference between a Doctor of Nursing Practice (DNP) and a PhD in Nursing. The DNP degree is generally more focused on:
source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Focused mainly on administrative and organizational leadership roles across a facility, with a fairly limited direct clinical practice component built into the coursework","B":"A degree whose primary focus tends to be described in fairly vague or inconsistent terms across different nursing school programs and curricula","C":"Original research generation, in much the same structured way a traditional research-focused PhD program is typically designed","D":"Advanced clinical practice and applying evidence to improve clinical outcomes, while the PhD is generally more focused on generating new nursing knowledge through original research"}}
source_row.rationale: The DNP degree is generally more focused on advanced clinical practice and applying evidence-based knowledge to improve clinical outcomes, while the PhD in Nursing is generally more focused on generating new nursing knowledge.
source_row.source_name: AACN — DNP vs. PhD Nursing Degree Comparison
source_row.source_detail: Distinguishing DNP and PhD Focus Areas

source_row.stem: A nurse practitioner's scope of practice, including prescriptive authority and independence from physician oversight, can vary based on:
source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Mainly the individual nurse practitioner's own personal preference for how they would like to structure their independent practice","B":"A single federal standard that is applied the exact same way in every state without any local regulatory variation at all","C":"The specific state's regulations, which range from full practice authority to reduced or restricted practice depending on the state","D":"A regulatory landscape that is fairly undefined or left largely unaddressed by any state nursing board"}}
source_row.rationale: Nurse practitioner scope of practice varies significantly by state, ranging from full practice authority to reduced or restricted practice requiring physician collaboration or supervision.
source_row.source_name: NCSBN/AANP — Nurse Practitioner Scope of Practice by State
source_row.source_detail: State Variation in NP Practice Authority

source_row.stem: A Clinical Nurse Specialist (CNS) role typically focuses on:
source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"A role fairly similar to a general staff nurse position, without much additional graduate-level advanced clinical preparation involved","B":"Mostly administrative duties within the unit, with a fairly limited hands-on clinical component to the everyday work","C":"Advanced expertise in a specialty area, often influencing care through direct practice, education, consultation, and system-level quality improvement","D":"Direct primary care management structured in much the same way a nurse practitioner's independent practice role typically is"}}
source_row.rationale: The Clinical Nurse Specialist role typically focuses on advanced expertise within a specialty area, influencing care through direct practice, staff education, consultation, and system-level quality improvement.
source_row.source_name: National Association of Clinical Nurse Specialists — CNS Role Definition
source_row.source_detail: Scope of the Clinical Nurse Specialist Role
